tools.name: Read
tools.description: Reads a file from the local filesystem. The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path. By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file. You can optionally specify a line offset and limit. Any lines longer than 2000 characters will be truncated. You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. It is always better to speculatively read multiple files as a batch that are potentially useful.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from

limit.description: The number of lines to read

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacements in files.

Usage:
- You must use your Read tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- Always use absolute paths.
- The edit will FAIL if `old_string` is not unique in the file.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

tools.name: Bash
tools.description: Executes a given bash command with optional timeout. Before executing the command, ensure that the parent directory exists. Avoid using it for file reads; use dedicated tools instead. NEVER update the git config. Do not run destructive commands such as `git reset --hard` unless the user explicitly asks.
